subject: Urban Planning
title: Car-Free Districts: Reclaiming Streets
description: A 60-second lesson on Car-Free Districts: Reclaiming Streets.

hook.text: Vauban in Freiburg, Germany is a car-free neighborhood of 5,500 residents. Streets belong to children, cyclists, and walkers.

buildup.text: Residents can own a car but must park it in a garage at the neighborhood edge. Inside, no cars are allowed on streets.

discovery.text: Car ownership in Vauban is 150 per 1,000 residents — compared to 800 per 1,000 in typical US suburbs.

twist.text: Property values in car-free neighborhoods are higher than car-dependent ones. People pay a premium for quiet, safe streets.

climax.text: Barcelona's superblocks close interior streets to through-traffic, creating car-free plazas in every few blocks.

punchline.text: Remove the cars. The street becomes a park. Property values go up.

quiz.question: What happens to property values in car-free neighborhoods?
options: They decrease because residents can't park near their homes
They increase because people pay a premium for quiet, safe streets
They stay the same because car access doesn't affect property values
